_what: One row per CREATE-SHAPED capability on the agent surface. Each row either NAMES the tool that undoes it, or carries a `reason` saying why no reversal exists. This is CLAUDE.md's first never-compromise property written down: 'New capabilities ship with their reversal - create/delete, deploy/undeploy, install/uninstall - or they state plainly why reversal is impossible.' Enforced by tests/sop/reversibility-ledger.test.ts.
_rules: A create-shaped tool with no row fails the build. Adding the tool means answering the question.
`reverses` names a tool that EXISTS. A row pointing at a tool nobody registered is stale and fails.
`reason` is for a capability that genuinely cannot be undone, or whose reversal is a product decision nobody has taken. It is not a way to skip the question - the text is read by a person.
A `reason` row is a DEBT, not a resolution. The set of them should shrink, and the enforcer pins it so it cannot grow silently.

The reversal need not share a verb stem. `deploy_mesh` is undone by `delete_mesh`, `publish_page` by `delete_page`. A naming rule was measured and REJECTED - it wrongly flags at least three - see PL-55's design section.
_measured: 2026-09-10: 109 tools across both registration forms, read via tests/sop/tool.testUtils.ts (`src/features/ai/server/*.ts`, `src/mcp-server.ts`, `src/mcp/*.ts`). 15 create-shaped. An earlier hand-rolled walk read only one directory and found 100 - the shared helper exists because that mistake has now been made twice.

entries.note: An ERP added from the integration's card is removed on its own: the integration stops listing it, its records are wiped, it is undeployed and its workspace deleted (AB-16).

Added 2026-10-03. The same creation as create_project, seeded from an exported file, so the same tool undoes it. It deploys the integrations the file names, which delete_project tears down with the project.

entries.reason: Added 2026-10-03, when the tool grew to cover headless projects (it was reset_eds_project). A reset IS the return to zero this property asks for, so nothing undoes it: what it discards - hand edits to the storefront repository, its DA.live content, or a headless project's component folders - exists nowhere else to restore from. That is why it asks first (confirm:true and the consent dialog) and why integrations, whose code may be the SC's own, are left alone. Not create-shaped, so the enforcer would not have asked; written down because the owner did. Snapshot-before-reset would be the reversal, and whether to build one is an owner decision.

entries.note: Different verb stem, deliberately: the mesh is deleted rather than undeployed. This row is why the enforcer pairs by ledger and not by name.

remove_integration undeploys it remotely, then cleans up that integration's files and keyed state. AB-7 is an open defect in exactly this reversal - it reported success while leaving deployed code running - which is what an unenforced principle looks like in production.
install_integration re-runs the Commerce install/associate pass for an already-deployed integration; remove_integration uninstalls it from Commerce before undeploying.

delete_page unpublishes AND deletes the source, so it is a WIDER reversal than publish_page's exact inverse - there is no unpublish-but-keep-source tool. Recorded because the published state can be undone; narrowing it is a product question, not a defect.

entries.reason: DECIDED 2026-09-11 (owner): uninstall should NOT exist. Node, the aio CLI and its plugins are machine-level tools an SC almost certainly uses outside this extension; removing them because a demo ended is a worse outcome than the asymmetry. This is a stated decision, not an open question.

entries.note: Corrected 2026-09-11: the first pass recorded this as having no reversal. set_console_apis sets the subscriptions to EXACTLY a list -- 'anything currently subscribed and not listed is REMOVED, pass an empty array to clear the extras' -- so it is the un-add. The handbook already described it as 'a delete wearing a setter's name'. Recording a gap without checking whether the capability already existed is how a ledger becomes fiction.

entries.reason: A sign-in, not a created resource - nothing is provisioned that could be deleted, so reversibility does not apply. DECIDED 2026-09-11 (owner): whether an agent should be able to sign you OUT is a question about agent power rather than about undo, and is out of scope for this ledger.

Writes into the SHARED datapack catalog, so the reversal is not merely a delete - it would have to consider other consumers. DECIDED 2026-09-11 (owner): design it now. Note the boundary - the catalog is owned by the data-installer service, so the design may conclude the reversal does not live in this repo.

entries.note: Corrected 2026-09-11, same mistake: reset_datapack removes a datapack's data from the Commerce instance so the project can be reused, which is precisely what the import put there. The first pass called it 'adjacent' without reading its description.
The demo ERP's simulated downtime also ends by itself when its minutes are up (AB-59).

Added 2026-10-03 with the tool (AB-6), at the owner's ask - not create-shaped, so the enforcer would not have asked. The providers it can delete are the open workspace's own 3rd-party custom providers, which in practice an App Management app (the Commerce starter kit) created at install; reinstall_integration uninstalls and installs the app again, and the install finds-or-creates every provider the app declares (.rptc/research/event-provider-lifecycle/research.md section 1.4 - read from the kit's source, not yet seen live). A provider made any other way (a hand-run aio onboarding, a custom app) has no reversal in this extension: the create tools were removed with the rest of the pulled surface in 4a3889049 and did not come back. Consent-gated for that reason.
